s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with cardiac structural abnormalities and a mass on the tricuspid leaflet
salient_findings: Antero-septal STEMI treated with primary PCI and stenting
Mild LV dilation and LVEF 46% due to anterior/mid-septal and apical akinesia
Mass on the ventricular surface of the anterior tricuspid leaflet
key_facts: Surgically repaired infra-renal abdominal aortic aneurysm
Unremarkable cardiovascular and respiratory findings on physical exam
Sclerotic aortic and mitral leaflets with mild AR and moderate MR
Mass on the ventricular surface of the anterior tricuspid leaflet is ~9 mm round and hyperechoic
TEE confirmed a 6×8 mm non-solid structure on the ventricular aspect of the anterior tricuspid leaflet
Contrast-enhanced chest CT excluded pulmonary embolism

shortlist.label: Papillary fibroelastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass on the tricuspid leaflet with characteristic 'finger-in-glove' appearance on TEE

shortlist.label: Lambl's excrescences
shortlist.why_kept: Small, filamentous structures on valve leaflets, consistent with patient's asymptomatic presentation

shortlist.label: Tricuspid valve fibroelastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location and description of mass on tricuspid leaflet, similar to papillary fibroelastoma

shortlist.label: Infective endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Although blood cultures were negative, valve abnormalities and mass could be related to infectious process

shortlist.label: Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of valve abnormalities and mass, with patient's history of malignancy risk factors (e.g., smoking)

raw.rationale: The description of a ~9 mm round, hyperechoic mass adherent to the ventricular surface of the anterior tricuspid leaflet with a 'finger-in-glove' appearance and 'garland-like' echogenicity on TEE is characteristic of papillary fibroelastoma, a benign cardiac tumor.

rejected.label: Lambl's excrescences
rejected.why: Lambl's excrescences are typically smaller and less complex than the described mass.

rejected.label: Tricuspid valve fibroelastoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific location and description provided do not exclusively point to the tricuspid valve as the primary site, making Papillary fibroelastoma a more encompassing diagnosis.

rejected.label: Infective endocarditis
rejected.why: Negative blood cultures and the absence of other signs of infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis
rejected.why: The patient's asymptomatic status and the specific echocardiographic findings do not align well with non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis, which is often associated with systemic diseases like cancer or sepsis.
